[0] At today's September event, Apple officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, but did not simultaneously announce the standard iPhone 18. The reasons will be explained shortly.

[1] The standard iPhone 18 is expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple has adjusted the release schedule for its new products.

[2] Generally speaking, today's Apple event should have been called the "iPhone 18 launch event."

[3] However, Apple's arrangement caught many people off guard — they did not launch the iPhone 18 today, at least not the standard version.

[4] This time, Apple only unveiled three high-end new iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

[5] This flagship lineup is clearly different from Apple's previous practice: in the past, new standard iPhones were always announced alongside the Pro models. However, as early as May 2025, there were already related reports foreshadowing this change.

[6] According to multiple reports, the three new iPhones Apple launched today will be joined by three more new devices in early 2027:

  • [7] iPhone 18
  • [8] iPhone 18e
  • [9] iPhone Air 2

[10] So the standard iPhone 18 has not been cancelled — it is just being released later than usual.

[11] Why is there this change?

[12] One explanation is that Apple wants to expand the iPhone product line through new models such as the Duo foldable phone, and does not want to launch too many products all at once in the fall. Splitting the release of major iPhones into fall and spring cycles may be more advantageous.

[13] Another possible reason is that Apple foresaw the current memory shortage early on, knowing that launching the standard iPhone 18 simultaneously with the Pro and Duo models would make it difficult to meet market demand.

[14] Regardless, the iPhone 18 will eventually arrive — it will just have to wait until early 2027.

[15] What are your thoughts on Apple's strategy of splitting the iPhone 18 lineup into two phases? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
